_comment: UHS overrides to HPG's region/period table, applied after it by scripts/port-name-kits.ts. `replace` drops every HPG window for that region and uses these instead; `add` keeps HPG's and merges these in, clipping any HPG window that overlaps. Keys are UHS region ids as they appear in name-regions.generated.ts. Windows are [from, to), astronomical years, half-open.

european-ural-mountains.why: HPG gave the whole Urals Scandinavian names for 200-1200 and proto-Germanic before that, which is 2000 km and a language family out. The middle and northern Urals are Permic and Ob-Ugric country, with Turkic pressure from the south after the Bulgar and Horde periods.

european-ural-and-arctic-europe.why: Same fault further north. This is Nenets, Komi and Sami country; Russian settlement follows the sixteenth century.

european-lapland.why: HPG gave Lapland proto-Germanic and then Scandinavian. Sapmi is Sami; Nordic names arrive with church and state registration.

european-scandinavia.why: The Viking age and the high Middle Ages were running on a modern Swedish pool. Old Norse covers 750-1400; the modern pool is now clamped to 1700.

european-atlantic-islands.why: Iceland and the Faroes were uninhabited before the ninth century, so the window should start at settlement rather than at the beginning of time.

european-british-isles.why: Scandinavian settlement in the Danelaw and the Isles was Old Norse-speaking, not modern Swedish.

east-asian-japan.why: One window from the beginning of time to the present, on a pool of Meiji-era surnames. Japan was settled deep in the Palaeolithic but its onomastics are not recoverable before the written record.

southeast-asian-indochina-interior.why: Angkor was running on modern Cambodian names with Sino-Cambodian surnames.

east-asian-kazakh-steppes.why: Ottoman names were standing in for the Turk and Uyghur khaganates and the whole pre-Mongol steppe.

east-asian-xinjiang.why: As the Kazakh steppes; the Uyghur khaganate and its successors are the Old Turkic case proper.
